content: The mandibular and hyoid arches exhibit a more rapid growth compared to the arches located posterior to them. As a result of this differential growth, the posterior arches become somewhat telescoped within the anterior ones. This anatomical arrangement leads to the formation of a pronounced depression on each side of the neck, referred to as the cervical sinus. The cervical sinus is anatomically defined by its boundaries: anteriorly, it is bordered by the hyoid arch, while posteriorly, it is limited by the thoracic wall. Over time, the cervical sinus is obliterated as its walls fuse together, eliminating the depression. Additionally, this process can be observed in the ventral view of a 32-day-old human embryo, where the head and neck structures are visible.
